title: Why normal energy becomes small near a tangential characteristic
reviewed_arguments: All 19 original obligations, 21 displays, 17 labelled equations and both complete solutions are preserved. The historical staged source has identical mathematical sections.

The divergence-form operator is +partial_x(a partial_x); the normal coefficient derivative is included. Compact upper support and either zero value or zero conormal derivative at zero remove the actual boundary product.
The unitary convention is derived from the exact prior F/G maps and pairing, with all powers of 2pi cancelled. Uniform Schwartz seminorms and M4 justify parameter derivatives and product integration.

The explicit smooth multiplier is zero near time frequency zero and equals its inverse absolute value on the actual support. Bounded derivatives preserve Schwartz seminorms. It commutes with all normal and tangential derivatives and x-only coefficients, keeps both supports and both boundary conditions, and is self-adjoint by the proved pairing.

Positive B(0) bounds tangential momentum by 2tau squared/b0. The coefficient-freezing bound uses only an upper bound, not positivity of the varying tangential defect. Theta includes both cone and collar widths.
The exact normal derivative estimate retains the transformed source norm and arbitrary positive gamma. Theta zero is not used as a divisor; no singular endpoint parameter choice is made.

Substitution h=omega=epsilon delta yields K=(2+2C/b0)/a0 and the exact source square. Mixed absorption uses the proved Hilbert Cauchy-Schwarz and Young square and retains M squared/(2a0 beta squared epsilon cubed delta), including M=0.

Uniform regularization families require the same hypotheses and source bounds at fixed localization widths. No shrinking-width uniform estimate or variable tangential coefficient commutator estimate is claimed.

The frequency packet is constructed inside a nonempty strict hyperbolic region, with an explicit interior point for positive omega and d at least one; d=0,omega=1 is treated. Omega zero cannot supply that packet. The normal cutoff is an explicit smooth step and preserves the Dirichlet condition.

The entire cutoff source is computed, including both derivatives. The ODE energy calculation proves nonzero source for a nonzero compact normal packet, with complete zero-data uniqueness. Both original source-weight exercises are unchanged.
The exact affine figure distinguishes upper-bound coefficients from solution energies, marks h=0 as a limit and explicitly retains the separate source term.
